title: POLARIS: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Mitigating Power Side-Channel Leakage
problem: Microelectronic systems handling sensitive data (encryption keys) are vulnerable to power side-channel attacks that infer secrets through dynamic power profiles; current mitigation solutions suffer from high overhead or incomplete leakage reduction.
motivation: Power side-channel attacks pose a critical threat to security-sensitive systems; XAI-guided mitigation can enable targeted, efficient defenses while maintaining visibility into protection mechanisms.
method: POLARIS framework uses Explainable AI (XAI) to guide a masking-based mitigation approach. Employs unsupervised process to automatically build tailored training datasets without manual labeling. Trains a masking model on this dataset to obfuscate power signatures. XAI guidance enables targeting the most exploitable power patterns for efficient mitigation.
key_novelty: First XAI-guided framework for automated power side-channel mitigation, enabling interpretable and efficient masking without manual attack expertise.
contributions: Unsupervised dataset generation for tailored threat models
Outperforms VALIANT and other state-of-the-art mitigations in leakage reduction
Lower execution time and area overhead across large designs

metrics.other: Leakage reduction, execution time overhead, area overhead

limitations: Evaluation focused on power side-channels; applicability to other side-channel vectors (timing, EM) and resistance to adaptive attacks not discussed.
